questions.stem: At $298\ \text{K}$, the standard enthalpy of formation of $\text{H}_2\text{O}(l)$ is $-286\ \text{kJ}\ \text{mol}^{-1}$. The standard enthalpy of combustion of carbon (graphite) is $-393.5\ \text{kJ}\ \text{mol}^{-1}$ and the standard enthalpy of combustion of liquid ethanol is $-1366.8\ \text{kJ}\ \text{mol}^{-1}$. The standard enthalpy of formation of liquid ethanol ($\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{OH}$) is $-x\ \text{kJ}\ \text{mol}^{-1}$. The value of $x$ is _______. (Nearest Integer)
questions.solution:
Reaction of combustion of ethanol:
$\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{OH}(l) + 3\text{O}_2(g) \rightarrow 2\text{CO}_2(g) + 3\text{H}_2\text{O}(l)$
$\Delta H_c^{\circ} = [2\Delta_f H^{\circ}(\text{CO}_2) + 3\Delta_f H^{\circ}(\text{H}_2\text{O})] - \Delta_f H^{\circ}(\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{OH})$
$-1366.8 = [2(-393.5) + 3(-286.0)] - \Delta_f H^{\circ}(\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{OH})$
$-1366.8 = [-787.0 - 858.0] - \Delta_f H^{\circ}(\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{OH})$
$-1366.8 = -1645.0 - \Delta_f H^{\circ}(\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{OH})$
$\Delta_f H^{\circ}(\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{OH}) = -1645.0 + 1366.8 = -278.2\ \text{kJ}\ \text{mol}^{-1}$.
Thus, $x = 278$ (nearest integer).

questions.stem:
Given that:
$$\mathrm{C}(\text{graphite}) + \mathrm{O}_2(g) \rightarrow \mathrm{CO}_2(g) \quad \Delta H^\circ = -393.5\ \mathrm{kJ\ mol^{-1}}$$
$$\mathrm{CO}(g) + \frac{1}{2}\mathrm{O}_2(g) \rightarrow \mathrm{CO}_2(g) \quad \Delta H^\circ = -283.0\ \mathrm{kJ\ mol^{-1}}$$
The enthalpy of formation of $\mathrm{CO}(g)$ is:
questions.solution:
We want to find $\Delta_f H^\circ$ of $\mathrm{CO}(g)$:
$\mathrm{C}(\text{graphite}) + \frac{1}{2}\mathrm{O}_2(g) \rightarrow \mathrm{CO}(g)$
Let Equation (1): $\mathrm{C} + \mathrm{O}_2 \rightarrow \mathrm{CO}_2$, $\Delta H_1 = -393.5\ \mathrm{kJ\ mol^{-1}}$
Let Equation (2): $\mathrm{CO} + \frac{1}{2}\mathrm{O}_2 \rightarrow \mathrm{CO}_2$, $\Delta H_2 = -283.0\ \mathrm{kJ\ mol^{-1}}$
Subtracting Eq (2) from Eq (1):
$\mathrm{C}(\text{graphite}) + \frac{1}{2}\mathrm{O}_2(g) \rightarrow \mathrm{CO}(g)$
$\Delta_f H^\circ = \Delta H_1 - \Delta H_2 = -393.5 - (-283.0) = -110.5\ \mathrm{kJ\ mol^{-1}}$.

questions.stem: Identify the reaction for which $\Delta H = \Delta U$ at constant temperature:
questions.solution:
We know $\Delta H = \Delta U + \Delta n_g R T$. For $\Delta H = \Delta U$, we must have $\Delta n_g = 0$.
For $\mathrm{C(s)} + \mathrm{O}_2\mathrm{(g)} \rightarrow \mathrm{CO}_2\mathrm{(g)}$, $\Delta n_g = 1 - 1 = 0$. Since carbon is in solid form, only gaseous reactants and products are counted.

questions.stem:
For the reaction
$2\mathrm{H}_2(\mathrm{g}) + \mathrm{O}_2(\mathrm{g}) \rightarrow 2\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}(\mathrm{l})$
$\Delta H^{\circ} = -572\ \mathrm{kJ}$.
The heat of decomposition of water per mole (in $\mathrm{kJ}$) is __________.
questions.solution:
The given thermochemical equation is:
$2\mathrm{H}_2(\mathrm{g}) + \mathrm{O}_2(\mathrm{g}) \rightarrow 2\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}(\mathrm{l}) \quad \Delta H^{\circ} = -572\ \mathrm{kJ}$
For the decomposition of 2 moles of water:
$2\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}(\mathrm{l}) \rightarrow 2\mathrm{H}_2(\mathrm{g}) + \mathrm{O}_2(\mathrm{g}) \quad \Delta H^{\circ} = +572\ \mathrm{kJ}$
Therefore, the heat of decomposition per mole of water is:
$\frac{572}{2} = 286\ \mathrm{kJ}$.

questions.stem: For a chemical reaction $3A + 2B \rightarrow 5C$, the relation between standard enthalpy change $\Delta H^{\circ}$ and standard internal energy change $\Delta U^{\circ}$ is given by :
questions.solution:
Assuming all reactants and products are in the gaseous state:
$\Delta n_g = n_p - n_r = 5 - (3+2) = 0$.
Since $\Delta H^{\circ} = \Delta U^{\circ} + \Delta n_g RT$, with $\Delta n_g = 0$, we get $\Delta H^{\circ} = \Delta U^{\circ}$.

questions.stem:
For the reaction $2 \text{H}_{2}(\text{g}) + \text{O}_{2}(\text{g}) \rightarrow 2 \text{H}_{2}\text{O}(\text{g})$, the standard enthalpy change, $\Delta H^{\circ} = -483.64\text{ kJ}$. What is the standard internal energy change $\Delta U^{\circ}$ for the reaction at $298\text{ K}$ in $\text{ kJ}$? (Nearest integer)
[Given: $R = 8.314\text{ J K}^{-1}\text{ mol}^{-1}$]
questions.solution:
$\Delta n_g = n_p - n_r = 2 - (2+1) = -1$.
$\Delta H^{\circ} = \Delta U^{\circ} + \Delta n_g RT \implies \Delta U^{\circ} = \Delta H^{\circ} - \Delta n_g RT$
$\Delta U^{\circ} = -483.64\text{ kJ} - (-1) \times (8.314 \times 10^{-3}\text{ kJ K}^{-1}\text{ mol}^{-1}) \times 298\text{ K}$
$\Delta U^{\circ} = -483.64 + 2.478 = -481.16\text{ kJ}$.
Nearest integer value is $-481$.

questions.stem: The enthalpy of combustion of carbon, hydrogen, and sucrose at $298\ \mathrm{K}$ are $-393.5\ \mathrm{kJ\ mol^{-1}}$, $-285.8\ \mathrm{kJ\ mol^{-1}}$, and $-5644.0\ \mathrm{kJ\ mol^{-1}}$ respectively. The enthalpy of formation of sucrose $(\mathrm{C_{12}H_{22}O_{11}})$ is:
questions.solution:
Reaction: $12\mathrm{C(s)} + 11\mathrm{H_2(g)} + 5.5\mathrm{O_2(g)} \rightarrow \mathrm{C_{12}H_{22}O_{11}(s)}$.
$\Delta_f H^{\circ} = 12\Delta_c H^{\circ}(\mathrm{C}) + 11\Delta_c H^{\circ}(\mathrm{H_2}) - \Delta_c H^{\circ}(\text{sucrose})$
$= 12(-393.5) + 11(-285.8) - (-5644.0)$
$= -4722.0 - 3143.8 + 5644.0 = -2221.8\ \mathrm{kJ\ mol^{-1}}$.

questions.stem:
For the reaction $A(g) \to B(g)$, the value of the equilibrium constant at $298\ \mathrm{K}$ is $100$. The value of standard Gibbs free energy change, $\Delta G^\circ$ for the reaction at $298\ \mathrm{K}$ is $- X \times 10^{-1}\ \mathrm{kJ\ mol^{-1}}$. The value of $X$ is _____. (Nearest integer)
[Use: $R = 8.314\ \mathrm{J\ K^{-1}\ mol^{-1}}$, $\ln 10 = 2.3$]
questions.solution:
$\Delta G^\circ = -RT \ln K = -8.314 \times 298 \times \ln(100) \ 
= -8.314 \times 298 \times 2 \times 2.3 = -11396.8\ \mathrm{J\ mol^{-1}} = -11.4\ \mathrm{kJ\ mol^{-1}}$.
Comparing with $-X \times 10^{-1}\ \mathrm{kJ\ mol^{-1}}$:
$-11.4\ \mathrm{kJ\ mol^{-1}} = -114 \times 10^{-1}\ \mathrm{kJ\ mol^{-1}} \implies X = 114$.

questions.stem:
For a reaction, $\text{A}(g) \rightarrow \text{B}(g)$, the value of equilibrium constant at $300\ \text{K}$ is $100$. The value of $\Delta G^{\circ}$ for the reaction at the same temperature is:
(Given: $R = 8.314\ \text{J K}^{-1}\ \text{mol}^{-1}$)
questions.solution:
Using the relation:
$\Delta G^{\circ} = -2.303 RT \log_{10} K$
$\Delta G^{\circ} = -2.303 \times 8.314 \times 300 \times \log_{10}(100)$
$\Delta G^{\circ} = -2.303 \times 8.314 \times 300 \times 2 = -11488.2\ \text{J mol}^{-1} \approx -11.5\ \text{kJ mol}^{-1}$.

questions.stem: For the reaction $C(s) + O_2(g) \rightarrow CO_2(g)$, $\Delta H^{\circ} = -393\ \mathrm{kJ\ mol^{-1}}$. The amount of heat released when $3.0\ \mathrm{g}$ of carbon is burnt in excess oxygen is _________ $\mathrm{kJ}$. (Round off to the nearest integer)
questions.solution:
Moles of carbon burnt = $\frac{3.0}{12.0} = 0.25\ \mathrm{mol}$.
Heat released = $0.25 \times 393\ \mathrm{kJ} = 98.25\ \mathrm{kJ}$.
Rounding off to the nearest integer gives $98$.

questions.stem:
For the reaction
$2\mathrm{H}_2(g) + \mathrm{O}_2(g) \rightarrow 2\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}(g)$;
$\Delta H^{\circ} = -483.6\ \mathrm{kJ}$.
If the bond enthalpies of $\mathrm{H}-\mathrm{H}$ and $\mathrm{O}=\mathrm{O}$ bonds are $436\ \mathrm{kJ\ mol^{-1}}$ and $496\ \mathrm{kJ\ mol^{-1}}$ respectively, then the average bond enthalpy of $\mathrm{O}-\mathrm{H}$ bond in $\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}$ is _________ $\mathrm{kJ\ mol^{-1}}$. (Round off to the nearest integer)
questions.solution:
$\Delta H = \sum B.E.\text{(reactants)} - \sum B.E.\text{(products)}$
$-483.6 = [2 \times B.E.(\mathrm{H}-\mathrm{H}) + B.E.(\mathrm{O}=\mathrm{O})] - 4 \times B.E.(\mathrm{O}-\mathrm{H})$
$-483.6 = [2(436) + 496] - 4 \times B.E.(\mathrm{O}-\mathrm{H})$
$-483.6 = 1368 - 4 \times B.E.(\mathrm{O}-\mathrm{H})$
$4 \times B.E.(\mathrm{O}-\mathrm{H}) = 1368 + 483.6 = 1851.6$
$B.E.(\mathrm{O}-\mathrm{H}) = 462.9\ \mathrm{kJ\ mol^{-1}} \approx 463$.

questions.stem:
The standard heat of formation of $\mathrm{U_3O_8(s)}$ is $-3575\ \mathrm{kJ\ mol^{-1}}$ and that of $\mathrm{UO_2(s)}$ is $-1085\ \mathrm{kJ\ mol^{-1}}$. For the reaction
$3\mathrm{UO_2(s)} + \mathrm{O_2(g)} \rightarrow \mathrm{U_3O_8(s)}$
the enthalpy change is _________ $\mathrm{kJ}$.
questions.solution:
$\Delta H^{\circ}_{rxn} = \Delta H^{\circ}_f(\mathrm{U_3O_8}) - [3 \times \Delta H^{\circ}_f(\mathrm{UO_2}) + \Delta H^{\circ}_f(\mathrm{O_2})]$
$\Delta H^{\circ}_{rxn} = -3575 - [3(-1085) + 0]$
$\Delta H^{\circ}_{rxn} = -3575 - (-3255) = -320\ \mathrm{kJ}$.

questions.stem: The standard enthalpy of combustion of glucose, $\mathrm{C_6H_{12}O_6(s)}$ at $298\ \mathrm{K}$ is $-2800\ \mathrm{kJ\ mol^{-1}}$. If the standard enthalpies of formation of $\mathrm{CO_2(g)}$ and $\mathrm{H_2O(l)}$ are $-393\ \mathrm{kJ\ mol^{-1}}$ and $-286\ \mathrm{kJ\ mol^{-1}}$ respectively, the standard enthalpy of formation of glucose is $-x\ \mathrm{kJ\ mol^{-1}}$. The value of $x$ is ________. (Nearest integer)
questions.solution:
Combustion of glucose: $\mathrm{C_6H_{12}O_6(s)} + 6\mathrm{O_2(g)} \rightarrow 6\mathrm{CO_2(g)} + 6\mathrm{H_2O(l)}$
$\Delta_c H^\circ = [6\Delta_f H^\circ(\mathrm{CO_2}) + 6\Delta_f H^\circ(\mathrm{H_2O})] - [\Delta_f H^\circ(\mathrm{glucose}) + 0]$
$-2800 = [6(-393) + 6(-286)] - \Delta_f H^\circ(\mathrm{glucose})$
$-2800 = [-2358 - 1716] - \Delta_f H^\circ(\mathrm{glucose}) = -4074 - \Delta_f H^\circ(\mathrm{glucose})$
$\Delta_f H^\circ(\mathrm{glucose}) = -4074 + 2800 = -1274\ \mathrm{kJ\ mol^{-1}}$.
Thus, $x = 1274$.

questions.stem:
Using the following data:
$\text{C}(s, \text{graphite}) + \text{O}_2(g) \rightarrow \text{CO}_2(g); \Delta H^\circ = -393.5\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$
$\text{H}_2(g) + \frac{1}{2}\text{O}_2(g) \rightarrow \text{H}_2\text{O}(l); \Delta H^\circ = -285.8\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$
$\text{CO}_2(g) + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}(l) \rightarrow \text{CH}_4(g) + 2\text{O}_2(g); \Delta H^\circ = +890.3\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$
The standard enthalpy of formation of $\text{CH}_4(g)$ is _______ $\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$. (Nearest integer with sign)
questions.solution:
The formation reaction of methane is: $\text{C}(s, \text{graphite}) + 2\text{H}_2(g) \rightarrow \text{CH}_4(g)$.
We combine the reactions:
$\Delta H_f^\circ = \Delta H_1^\circ + 2\Delta H_2^\circ + \Delta H_3^\circ$
$\Delta H_f^\circ = -393.5 + 2(-285.8) + 890.3 = -393.5 - 571.6 + 890.3 = -74.8\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$.
Rounding to the nearest integer, we get -75.

questions.stem: For the combustion of one mole of liquid ethanol ($\mathrm{C_2H_5OH}$) at $298\ \mathrm{K}$ to form gaseous carbon dioxide and liquid water, the difference between the enthalpy of reaction ($\Delta H$) and the change in internal energy ($\Delta U$) (i.e., $\Delta H - \Delta U$) in $\mathrm{kJ\ mol^{-1}}$ is (Take $R = 8.314\ \mathrm{J\ K^{-1}\,mol^{-1}}$):
questions.solution:
The balanced chemical equation is:
$\mathrm{C_2H_5OH(l) + 3O_2(g) \rightarrow 2CO_2(g) + 3H_2O(l)}$
$\Delta n_g = n_g(\text{products}) - n_g(\text{reactants}) = 2 - 3 = -1$.
Since $\Delta H - \Delta U = \Delta n_g RT$,
$\Delta H - \Delta U = (-1) \times 8.314 \times 10^{-3}\ \mathrm{kJ\ K^{-1}\,mol^{-1}} \times 298\ \mathrm{K} = -2.48\ \mathrm{kJ\ mol^{-1}}$.

questions.stem:
For the reaction at $298\text{ K}$,
$\text{A}(g) + \text{B}(g) \rightarrow \text{C}(g) + \text{D}(g)$
$\Delta H^\circ = -29.8\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$ and $\Delta S^\circ = -0.100\text{ kJ K}^{-1}\text{ mol}^{-1}$. The value of $\Delta G^\circ$ for the reaction at $298\text{ K}$ is _______________ $\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$.
questions.solution:
Using $\Delta G^\circ = \Delta H^\circ - T\Delta S^\circ$:
$\Delta G^\circ = -29.8 - (298 \times -0.100) = -29.8 + 29.8 = 0$.

questions.stem: For the combustion of one mole of liquid ethanol ($\mathrm{C_2H_5OH}$) at $298\ \mathrm{K}$ and $1\ \mathrm{atm}$ pressure, $\Delta U = -1364\ \mathrm{kJ\ mol^{-1}}$. The value of enthalpy of combustion, $\Delta H$, for this reaction is $-x\ \mathrm{kJ\ mol^{-1}}$. The value of $x$ is _________. (Round off to the nearest integer) [Given: $R = 8.314\ \mathrm{J\ K^{-1}\ mol^{-1}}$]
questions.solution:
Combustion equation: $\mathrm{C_2H_5OH(l)} + 3\mathrm{O_2(g)} \rightarrow 2\mathrm{CO_2(g)} + 3\mathrm{H_2O(l)}$
$\Delta n_g = n_{p(g)} - n_{r(g)} = 2 - 3 = -1$
$\Delta H = \Delta U + \Delta n_g RT = -1364 + (-1) \times 8.314 \times 10^{-3} \times 298$
$\Delta H = -1364 - 2.477 = -1366.477\ \mathrm{kJ\ mol^{-1}}$
Thus, $x \approx 1366$.
